text:
Alex Chen: Ran a perf sweep on sm86 yesterday; saw a sharp regression for some head_dim/seq_len combos. looks like the autotuner is falling back to the generic SDPA path for certain odd head sizes and seqlen 128-256.
Maya Singh: can you share the profile snippets? :eyes:
Alex Chen: pasted below — reproed on a model with head_dim=30, batch=1, seq=192, causal. nsys snippets:
```
Kernel                calls   total_time (ms)
flash_attn_v3_causal  2       1.42
sdpa_generic          6       4.87
flash_attn_v3_nc      0       0.00
```
Also raw timeline shows flash_attn used when head_dim % 32 == 0, otherwise sdpa_generic gets picked by the kernel picker probe miss.
Samir Patel: is this new behavior after the recent autotuner change? we rolled down v3 selector last week.
Alex Chen: yes — autotuner probe set reduced to speed up cold-start probe time. it no longer exercises many head_dim residues. picker treats unprobed combos as 'unknown' and picks a safe SDPA path which is slower for causal in many cases.
Juan Gomez: KV cache patterns could hide this in steady state since cache tends to produce longer effective seqs. but for short interactive requests with lots of cache hits, we land in that problematic seqlen window frequently.
Maya Singh: repro steps we used?
Alex Chen: shell:
```
python -m perf.runner --model=toy_v3 --head-dim=30 --seq-len=192 --batch=1 --causal --profile=nsys --repeat=50
```
and tune flags: `--autotune-probe=true --kernel-probe-buckets=default`
Ryan Liu: short-term mitigation ideas?
Samir Patel: could we remap odd head dims to the next aligned head (30->32) via a view/pad trick at runtime for kernel selection only? that avoids changing weights.
Alex Chen: padding trick is promising but has caveats w.r.t. quantized kernels and memory overhead when many models/pools coexist. Also need to ensure correctness with KV packing.
Juan Gomez: I think we also need to broaden the probe matrix: include head_dim residues (mod 8/16/32) and seqlen buckets (<=64, 65-128, 129-256, >256). The probe cost is small if we cache results per-model-per-GPU and don't probe on every cold-start.
Maya Singh: agree. also add hysteresis in picker: require two consecutive probes favoring new kernel before flipping production traffic. prevents flapping with noisy measurements.
Ryan Liu: what about batching heuristics interacting here? the batcher tends to coalesce short requests and can change observed seqlen distribution — could make probes stale.
Alex Chen: noted. propose we tie probe validity to observed seqlen histogram in the past N minutes and expire probes when distribution shifts beyond a threshold.
Samir Patel: timeline? I can fast-follow with a small change that expands probe buckets and stores decisions in model metadata. Alex + Maya to run canary on dedicated pool.
Alex Chen: I'll push a patch to kernel-picker, add head residue buckets and seqlen buckets, and implement hysteresis. Maya will own the canary rollout and perf dashboards.
deploy-bot: Canary job created: canary/flash-prefetch-gap-1719998888 -> https://ci.internal/canaries/1719998888 :white_check_mark:
Maya Singh: canary started, collecting traces. will post numbers in ~2 hours.
Juan Gomez: also adding a unit test that forces head_dim=30 for v3 selector to ensure we prefer flash path when probe indicates it's faster; else fallback documented.
Ryan Liu: small note: for on-prem/private installs with limited telemetry we should default to conservative behaviour but expose a flag to force padding remap.
Samir Patel: ack. i'll draft the RFC for probe matrix expansion and the opt-in remap flag.
Alex Chen: thanks all. follow-ups: Alex/Maya implement + canary, Samir drafts RFC, Juan writes regression test. tagging @everyone for visibility :shipit:
Maya Singh: :thumbsup:
Samir Patel: :rocket:
